item:ados-fragment.text: Ados Fragment. The Ados Fragment is an inscribed piece of stone recovered from the Whelgar's Excavation site in the Wetlands. Together with three companion shards, it forms the Goaz Stone, an ancient relic bearing enigmatic Titan inscriptions. Unearthed in the muddy trenches of Whelgar's Excavation, the Ados Fragment is one of four missing pieces required to reconstruct the Goaz Stone. Prior to raptors overrunning the dig site, Prospector Whelgar began translating the primary tablet, only to discover that the inscriptions broke off at crucial moments. The scattered pieces—named Ados, Modr, Golm, and Neru—were lost across the ruins, concealed within ancient containers and dirt mounds amidst prowling beasts.

item:agamand-family-axe.text: Agamand Family Axe. The Agamand Family Axe is an ancestral heirloom preserved within the Agamand family crypt in northern Tirisfal Glades. Once a martial symbol of the wealthy mill-owning dynasty, it is sought by Coleman Farthing to strip the undead family of their remaining dignity. Before the Third War, the Agamand dynasty reigned as prosperous landowners across the northern hills of Tirisfal Glades, maintaining vast mills and a private family crypt. The Agamand Family Axe rested among the ancestral arms entombed alongside deceased patriarchs and warriors, kept intact on underground weapon racks even as the Scourge overran the estate and slaughtered its inhabitants. When the Scourge raised the fallen Agamands as mindless thralls to the Lich King, their former servant Coleman Farthing survived—in undeath—with bitter hatred for his old masters. Farthing blames the family for his own demise and commissions Forsaken wanderers to enter the crypt, strip the weapon racks of the axe, sword, mace, and dagger, and erase the final vestiges of the Agamand heritage.

item:agamand-family-dagger.text: Agamand Family Dagger. The Agamand Family Dagger is an ancestral heirloom of the fallen Agamand dynasty, resting on weapon racks within their ancestral crypt in northern Tirisfal Glades. Coleman Farthing seeks this blade alongside the rest of their family arsenal to strip his former masters of their remaining legacy and honor. Before the Third War, the Agamand family maintained vast estates and grain mills across the rolling meadows of Tirisfal Glades. Like the rest of their lineage's armaments, the Agamand Family Dagger survived the devastation wrought by the Scourge, locked within the family crypt north of Agamand Mills. Protected by the restless, undead remnants of the household and mindless minions of the Lich King, the dagger represents the prestige and martial heritage that once elevated the family above their servants and tenants. For Coleman Farthing, a Forsaken residing at Brill who died in the Agamands' service, the blade represents bitter resentment rather than noble lineage. Holding the family directly responsible for his death, Farthing directs adventurers into the Agamand Family Crypt to recover the dagger along with the family sword, axe, and mace. In stripping these ancestral armaments from their tomb, Farthing aims to rob the now-Scourge patriarchs of their last vestiges of dignity and ensure the Agamand memory is utterly extinguished.

item:agamand-family-mace.text: Agamand Family Mace. The Agamand Family Mace is an ancestral heirloom preserved within the Agamand Family Crypt in northern Tirisfal Glades. Once a symbol of pride for a wealthy dynasty of northern Lordaeron, it has become an object of spiteful retribution sought by their former servant Coleman Farthing. Before the Third War, the Agamand family held extensive farmlands and windmills in the northern reaches of Tirisfal Glades. Like the rest of the regional aristocracy, they fell before the plague of undeath. The Agamands were reanimated as mindless thralls in service to the Lich King, wandering their ruined estate while their ancient family treasures remained locked within the depths of the family crypt. The Agamand Family Mace is stored among these weapons, an emblem of a forgotten lineage now reduced to shambling Scourge.

item:agamand-family-sword.text: Agamand Family Sword. The Agamand Family Sword is a tarnished ancestral blade kept inside the Agamand Family Crypt in northern Tirisfal Glades. Once a proud symbol of the wealthy mill-owning dynasty, it is sought by the Forsaken Coleman Farthing to erase the final vestiges of his former masters' legacy. Before the Third War, the Agamand dynasty held immense wealth and influence across the rolling mills of northern Tirisfal Glades. When the Scourge swept through Lordaeron, the family met a gruesome end, their bodies raised into mindless thralls of the Lich King. Their ancestral weapons, including the ceremonial family sword, were sealed away in the Agamand Family Crypt at the northern edge of the mills. Stripping these blades from their burial racks serves not merely as looting, but as a deliberate act to break whatever memory and noble standing remains of the fallen household.

item:alterac-granite.text: Alterac Granite. Alterac Granite is a prized, durable stone quarried from the mountainous terrain of northern Lordaeron, specifically around Darrow Hill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Revered by master stonecutters for its exceptional resilience and grain, it is chosen by King Magni Bronzebeard's royal mason to carve an enduring tribute for fallen soldiers. When King Magni Bronzebeard ordered a monument to commemorate Sully Balloo—a brave dwarven defender who perished in the tragedy at the Thandol Span—ordinary quarry stone would not do. Grand Mason Marblesten, tasked with sculpting the memorial in Ironforge, insisted on obtaining Alterac Granite. Renowned as one of the finest stones available across the Eastern Kingdoms, its legendary durability ensures that the likeness and memory of a fallen hero can endure untarnished for generations. Harvesting Alterac Granite is far from a simple errand. The stone rests around Darrow Hill in the northern reaches of the Hillsbrad Foothills, close to the ruined territories of Alterac. With the region rife with hostile wildlife, lurking syndicate brigands, and lingering strife, retrieving unblemished slabs of this pristine stone requires bold adventurers willing to venture deep into contested lands to secure it for Ironforge's artisans.

item:ambercorn.text: Ambercorn. Ambercorn is a sacred nut that falls from the tall, ancient trees scattered across Mulgore. Infused with natural magic, it serves as a vital reagent in tauren shamanic brews, most notably used to induce spiritual visions during youth trials. Gathered from beneath the sturdy boughs of Mulgore's great trees, ambercorns are more than ordinary nuts to the tauren. Rich with the spiritual vitality of the land, they hold latent magical properties that tauren mystics have understood and utilized for generations. Young hunters and wanderers learn early to keep their eyes on the grass beneath the canopy, honoring the Earth Mother's gifts that fall freely from above. In Bloodhoof Village, the seer Zarlman Two-Moons relies on ambercorn when preparing young tauren for the Rite of Vision. Combined with stones gathered from the plains' pristine water wells, ambercorn is steeped into the potent Water of the Seers. Consuming this ceremonial elixir before the ancestral flames allows an initiate's senses to shift, revealing a guiding spirit animal meant to lead them to their next destination.

item:amethyst-phial.text: Amethyst Phial. The Amethyst Phial is a delicate ceremonial vessel entrusted to young night elf adventurers by Corithras Moonrage in Dolanaar. It is crafted specifically to gather and preserve sacred waters from the premier moonwell beneath the Oracle Tree. Entrusted to initiates on Teldrassil, the Amethyst Phial is the final vessel used in the Crown of the Earth pilgrimage. Corithras Moonrage tasks travelers with carrying it to the far northwestern reaches of the boughs, nestled within the Oracle Glade. There, beneath the ancient canopy of the Oracle Tree, lies the island's first and most potent moonwell. The phial is carefully dipped into these radiant waters to draw out the essence of Elune's grace, allowing druids and priestesses to study and tend to the unpredictable growth of the World Tree.

item:ancient-moonstone-seal.text: Ancient Moonstone Seal. The Ancient Moonstone Seal is a powerful relic of Highborne sorcery forged long before the Sundering. Imbued with potent arcane binding magic, it served as the anchor holding the spirit of Asterion captive within the ruins of Bashal'Aran. Forged by Asterion's former master, the powerful Highborne sorcerer Athrikus Narassin, the Ancient Moonstone Seal was crafted to serve as an unbreakable metaphysical anchor. While the Well of Eternity still stood and Queen Azshara reigned, Athrikus used the artifact to bind Asterion's soul to the pillars of Bashal'Aran. Over ten millennia later, Asterion remained an incorporeal prisoner to its magic, unable to break the ward with any strength or spell he possessed.

item:barrow-key.text: Barrow Key. The Barrow Key is one of three druidic keys hidden within the Talon Den atop Stonetalon Peak. It is kept locked inside a barrow cache to guard the ancient treasures sealed within the den's hoard. Within the subterranean barrows of the Talon Den, night elf druids established elaborate wards to protect their relics from interlopers. The Barrow Key is one piece of this multi-layered lock, concealed inside a specialized cache hidden among the subterranean passages. Accessing it requires the Gatekeeper's Key, ensuring that only those with knowledge of the druids' defensive network can ever hope to claim it.

item:bathran-s-hair.text: Bathran's Hair. Bathran's Hair is a rare, delicate herb found among the ruins of Bathran's Haunt in northwestern Ashenvale. Celebrated in night elf lore for its potent restorative qualities, the plant is believed to mend afflictions of the spirit as well as the flesh. Grown in the shadows of the ancient ruins north of Maestra's Post, Bathran's Hair has long been valued by night elf healers. Unlike common medicinal flora that soothe simple physical wounds, this herb possesses restorative properties said to cure deep ailments of the spirit. When a young night elf in Astranaar falls victim to an insidious, unyielding sickness, the herbalist Orendil Broadleaf seeks strands of this rare plant to brew a vital remedy.

item:berard-s-journal.text: Berard's Journal. Berard's Journal is a collection of research notes penned by Apothecary Berard before he fell victim to Archmage Arugal's curse. Left behind in Pyrewood Village, the book documents Berard's study of an ancient plague that once wiped out the aquatic life of Lake Lordamere, making it highly valuable to the Royal Apothecary Society. Before Archmage Arugal unleashed his shadow magic across Silverpine Forest, Apothecary Berard was considered one of the Royal Apothecary Society's most promising minds. Stationed in Pyrewood Village, he focused his work on an ancient, virulent blight that had eradicated all aquatic life within Lake Lordamere centuries prior. When Arugal's curse gripped the settlement, Berard's mind was shattered, turning him into another mindless thrall. His detailed field notes remained behind on a bookshelf in his quarters at the Pyrewood Village Inn.

item:bingles-blastencapper.text: Bingles' Blastencapper. Bingles' Blastencapper is a specialized explosive device designed by the gnome pilot Bingles Blastenheimer. Lost when his gyrocopter plunged into the Loch, it was stolen by local troggs, endangering Bingles' plans to support the liberation of Gnomeregan. Bingles' Blastencapper represents the peak of pilot Bingles Blastenheimer's personal ordnance. Built to deliver decisive aerial strikes against the troggs and leper gnomes overruning Gnomeregan, the explosive was aboard his gyrocopter when mechanical failure sent him plummeting into the waters of the Loch. While Bingles survived, troggs infesting the lake's northern islands pillaged his wreckage and dragged the volatile weapon back to their camps. To Bingles, the Blastencapper is far more than simple salvage. The exiled gnomes are actively preparing to take back their radioactive home, and Bingles considers his gyrocopter and signature munitions vital components of the impending air assault. Recovering this ordnance prevents the indigenous troggs of Loch Modan from accidentally triggering a catastrophe and preserves a valuable weapon for the gnomish resistance.

item:bingles-hammer.text: Bingles' Hammer. Bingles' Hammer is an engineering tool belonging to Bingles Blastenheimer, an eccentric gnome aviator stranded in Loch Modan. After crashing his flying machine into the Loch, hostile troggs scavenged the hammer along with his other specialized gear. Bingles needs it recovered so he can repair his aircraft and aid the war effort to liberate Gnomeregan. When pilot Bingles Blastenheimer plunged into the waters of the Loch, his survival was only the first of his troubles. Troggs inhabiting the freshwater islands quickly raided the crash site, looting his specialized toolkit and high-potency explosives. Among the pilfered gear was his hammer, an indispensable implement for repairing the dented airframe and recalibrating the gyrocopter's mechanical assemblies. Without this essential tool and the rest of his equipment, Bingles remains thoroughly grounded, unable to fly support runs for the gnome liberation forces struggling to reclaim Gnomeregan.

item:bingles-screwdriver.text: Bingles' Screwdriver. Bingles' Screwdriver is an essential engineering tool belonging to Bingles Blastenheimer, a gnome pilot who crashed his gyrocopter into the waters of Loch Modan. Following the crash, native troggs plundered the wreckage, scattering Bingles' tool buckets and specialized gear across the loch's northern islands. When Bingles Blastenheimer plummeted into the Loch, he lost more than his flying machine—he lost the specialized equipment needed to repair it. Among the scattered gear was his trusty screwdriver, packed away inside one of several tool buckets snatched up by opportunistic troggs inhabiting the nearby isles. For an engineer stranded in the wilderness, fine adjustment tools like this screwdriver are irreplaceable, especially when assembling delicate gyrocopter mechanisms or handling volatile armaments. Bingles is not merely a recreational aviator; he serves a larger cause dedicated to liberating the fallen city of Gnomeregan from troggs and leper gnomes. His mission relies on combining flight mechanics with his volatile Blastencapper munitions to deliver an aerial assault against the subterranean menace. Recovering this screwdriver alongside his wrench and hammer is crucial for putting his gyrocopter back together and keeping the gnomish airborne counteroffensive alive.

item:bingles-wrench.text: Bingles' Wrench. Bingles' Wrench is a vital piece of gnomish engineering gear belonging to the pilot Bingles Blastenheimer. Lost when Bingles crash-landed his flying machine into the Loch, it was hauled off by the local troggs alongside the rest of his toolkit. After Bingles Blastenheimer crashed his gyrocopter into the placid waters of the Loch, his survival quickly turned into an ordeal. Troggs inhabiting the small northern islands raided the crash site, looting his specialized supplies and scattering his tools into various buckets across their camps. Bingles' Wrench is one of three critical hand tools needed alongside his high-yield Blastencapper explosives. Without it, Bingles has no hope of repairing his downed gyrocopter, stalling his planned aerial offensive to aid the exiled gnomes fighting to reclaim Gnomeregan.

item:black-claw-stout.text: Black Claw Stout. Black Claw Stout is a special drink prepared by Zardeth of the Black Claw beneath the streets of Stormwind. Concocted for a meddlesome nobleman, it is delivered under the guise of an ordinary tavern beverage.

item:black-feather-quill.text: Black Feather Quill. The Black Feather Quill is a sacred night elf relic used by the Druids of the Talon during their rites of hibernation and awakening. Stored within a dedicated chest in the Ban'ethil Barrow Den, it is one of several vital focuses needed to safely call slumbering druids back from the Emerald Dream. Night elf druidism relies on deeply attuned sacred items to navigate the threshold between the waking world and the Emerald Dream. The Black Feather Quill, along with the Raven Claw Talisman, the Sapphire of Sky, and the Rune of Nesting, forms the core set of ritual items required to break the delicate hibernation of the Druids of the Talon. Without these focuses, a slumbering druid risks remaining trapped within the Dream indefinitely, unable to rejoin their waking body. When corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs overran the Ban'ethil Barrow Den, the sacred chests housing these treasures fell into danger. Left unguarded in the winding depths, the relics had to be recovered swiftly by order of Athridas Bearmantle in Dolanaar before the captive druids were lost forever to the Dream.

item:bloodstone-choker.text: Bloodstone Choker. The Bloodstone Choker is a dark magical talisman crafted from bloodstone, originally held by the warlock mentor Gakin the Darkbinder. Stolen by a treacherous apprentice who fled to the Defias Brotherhood, it serves as a powerful ritual focus capable of piercing the void to draw forth and bind a Voidwalker. Carved from bloodstone, the choker possesses the latent mystical authority required to bridge the mortal world and the twisting shadows of the Twisting Nether. Once returned to Gakin, it is immediately put to the test in the crypts beneath the tavern. A warlock must channel the choker's magic at the underground summoning circle to rip a hostile Voidwalker from the void. Only by subduing the furious entity in direct combat while wielding the talisman can a practitioner prove the willpower necessary to command such a guardian.

item:blueleaf-tuber.text: Blueleaf Tuber. Blueleaf Tubers are exceptionally rare root vegetables that grow concealed beneath the thorny terrain of Razorfen Kraul. Prized across the world as an exotic culinary delicacy, they are almost impossible to locate with the naked eye. Though native to the Barrens, Blueleaf Tubers grow only in the subterranean depths beneath Razorfen Kraul. Concealed beneath the dense root systems and quilboar briars, they remain hidden to casual foragers. Despite their harsh growing conditions, they fetch an exorbitant price among wealthy gourmands and traders worldwide who savor their unique flavor. Because the roots cannot be easily spotted by surface dwellers, the enterprising goblin Mebok Mizzyrix in Ratchet devised an unusual harvesting method. By training native snufflenose gophers to detect the tubers by scent from fifty paces away, adventurers guided by specialized command sticks can unearth the roots from the soil before quilboar patrols catch wind of the intrusion.

item:bottle-of-moonshine.text: Bottle of Moonshine. A Bottle of Moonshine is a potent alcoholic spirit sold in the gloomy settlement of Darkshire. Barkeep Daniels of Lakeshire urgently seeks a bottle to help restock the town tavern as Blackrock orc incursions cut off regular supply shipments. Lakeshire stands besieged by the Blackrock clan, leaving its local innkeeper, Barkeep Daniels, in dire straits as regular supply caravans fail to arrive. To keep up morale among the town guards and beleaguered townsfolk, Daniels sends couriers across the southern kingdoms to gather regional specialties. Among these is a potent bottle of moonshine brewed and sold at the Scarlet Raven Tavern in neighboring Duskwood, where locals favor stiff drinks to ward off the encroaching dread of the woods.

item:bottom-of-gelkak-s-key.text: Bottom of Gelkak's Key. The Bottom of Gelkak's Key is one of three fragments of a shattered mechanical winding key belonging to the shipwrecked gnome pirate Gelkak Gyromast. After his vessel foundered off Darkshore, the piece was scavenged by the shoreline's native reef crawlers. When Gelkak Gyromast's ship was sunk by threshadons off the coast of Darkshore, the gnome was thrown ashore along with his belongings. Among his most prized possessions was the winding key used to activate his mechanical first mate. The key shattered on the coastal rocks into three distinct pieces, and local scavengers immediately descended upon the debris. The bottom piece of the key was snatched up by the aggressive crustaceans wandering the surf—specifically the reef and tide crawlers that pick through the detritus along the tideline.

item:branch-of-cenarius.text: Branch of Cenarius. The Branch of Cenarius is a sacred dryad relic stolen by the vile satyr Geltharis in eastern Ashenvale. Recovering this heirloom was the dying wish of the dryad Anilia, who perished defending it from the woods' corruptors. Revered by the daughters of Cenarius, the Branch of Cenarius represents both the blessing of the Forest Lord and the deep connection his dryads maintain with Ashenvale. The branch was held in high regard by the dryad sisters Anilia and Illiyana until a band of corrupt satyrs ambushed them. The satyr leader, Geltharis, seized the relic and mortally wounded Anilia near the tainted ruins of eastern Ashenvale. With her dying breaths, Anilia pointed northward toward the arch where Geltharis lurks, pleading for a champion to wrest the sacred bough from his claws and restore it to dryad hands at Forest Song.

item:bundle-of-hides.text: Bundle of Hides. A Bundle of Hides consists of cured skins collected from the beasts of the Barrens, bundled together for transport across central Kalimdor. Bound for the leatherworkers of Thunder Bluff, it serves as a straightforward courier shipment that introduces travelers to the Horde's wind rider flight network. The untamed plains of the Barrens are home to vast herds of kodo, prowling lions, and roving raptors. Hunters along the trade paths skin these creatures not only for meat and survival, but to supply city artisans. Without raw pelts from the wilds, settlements like Thunder Bluff would struggle to sustain their local leathercrafters, who transform dried skins into essential gear, pouches, armor, and bindings for the Horde. Transporting heavy goods overland through the Barrens and up into Mulgore is dangerous and slow, constantly threatened by roaming quilboar and centaur raiders. To speed delivery between the Crossroads and the tauren capital, couriers rely on Devrak's trained wyverns. Handing a bundle of hides to a wind rider courier demonstrates the sheer efficiency of air travel across Kalimdor's fractured terrain.

item:burning-blade-medallion.text: Burning Blade Medallion. The Burning Blade Medallion is a dark talisman carried by cultists lurking within the Valley of Trials. Guarded by dark magic in the depths of the Burning Blade Coven, it serves as direct proof of demonic corruption attempting to subvert the young warriors of Durotar. Discovered deep inside the winding caverns of the Burning Blade Coven, the medallion is held by Yarrog Baneshadow, an agent of the sinister Burning Blade cult. Identified through the divinations of Zureetha Fargaze, the trinket channels dark power amidst the cult's impish familiars and felstalkers. Striking down its bearer and seizing the medallion cuts short an insidious attempt to undermine the Horde's training grounds from within Durotar itself.

item:cache-of-zanzil-s-altered-mixture.text: Cache of Zanzil's Altered Mixture. The Cache of Zanzil's Altered Mixture is a stockpile of potent poison secured inside a locked chest at the Venture Company tower near the Sludge Fen. Named for the jungle troll witch doctor Zanzil, it serves as a critical target for the Shattered Hand in Orgrimmar. North of the Sludge Fen in the Barrens, the Venture Company keeps a tower outpost. A cache of an altered mixture bearing the name of the infamous troll witch doctor Zanzil sits locked inside Grand Foreman Puzik Gallywix's private strongbox at the summit of the tower. A poison has weakened everything in the tower, leaving its goblin inhabitants vulnerable to any intruder bold enough to strike.

item:cactus-apple.text: Cactus Apple. Cactus Apples are tough, moisture-rich fruits harvested from the rugged flora of Durotar's Valley of Trials. Flourishing in the arid desert heat, they are prized by local orcs as a rare, refreshing source of sustenance. The sun-scorched earth of Durotar offers little luxury, forcing its inhabitants to make use of whatever hardy plants survive the elements. Cactus apples grow in clusters around the thick cactuses dotting the Valley of Trials. While difficult to gather without catching a few thorns, the fruit provides vital hydration in the sweltering canyon. A local orc named Galgar gathers these fruits to prepare his signature Cactus Apple Surprise, a cooling confection that brings welcome relief to recruits enduring their harsh initial training.

item:candle-of-beckoning.text: Candle of Beckoning. The Candle of Beckoning is an enchanted ritual taper kept by the reclusive necromancer Gunther Arcanus on Brightwater Lake. Placing and lighting the candle upon an altar on a nearby islet summons forth a restless spirit known as Lillith Nefara. Found stored in a crate beside the solitary mage Gunther Arcanus on his island in Brightwater Lake, the Candle of Beckoning serves as an instrument in a dark ritual of summoning. Gunther is a fiercely independent undead sorcerer who broke free of the Lich King's command on his own, remaining wary of the Scourge and the Forsaken alike. To prove your loyalty is not to the Lich King, Gunther directs you to take one of these candles southwest to a smaller islet. There, set upon an old, bloodstained table, the candle's flame pierces the veil between worlds to awaken and beckon the dormant shade of Lillith Nefara, a powerful Scourge agent, so she may be destroyed.

item:cantation-of-manifestation.text: Cantation of Manifestation. The Cantation of Manifestation is a specialized arcane incantation written on a parchment scroll, used by mages to reveal unseen magical anomalies. In the Undercity, Anastasia Hartwell provides it to apprentices investigating invisible magical entities haunting Algernon's shop in the Apothecarium. The Cantation of Manifestation holds a focused spell designed to pierce magical veils and force incorporeal, invisible beings into the visible spectrum. Kept in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity near Anastasia Hartwell, the scroll is entrusted to capable mages tasked with containing rogue magical anomalies. When read aloud in an area suffering from arcane instability—such as Algernon's alchemical workshop in the Apothecarium—the words force stray rift spawns to materialize, allowing the caster to subdue and trap them within containment coffers for further study.

item:cask-of-merlot.text: Cask of Merlot. A Cask of Merlot is a barrel of fine red wine produced and sold in Stormwind City. It serves as one of several regional specialty liquors needed by the Lakeshire innkeeper during the supply shortages caused by the Blackrock orc invasion. Harvested and fermented in the heart of the kingdom, this Cask of Merlot comes straight from the cellars of the Galina Winery, nestled along the canals bordering Stormwind's Trade District. Winemaker Roberto Pupellyverbos manages the vintages there, catering to the capital's more refined palates. Unlike the harsh moonshine of Duskwood or the rustic spirits brewed in Elwynn, the merlot represents the refined craft of human vintners operating under the relative safety of the city walls. When the Blackrock clan invaded the Redridge Mountains, supply routes fell apart, cutting Lakeshire off from its standard merchant shipments. Facing parched and terrified locals, Barkeep Daniels tasks willing couriers with undertaking a kingdom-wide run to restock his tavern's cellars. Procuring this cask ensures the defenders and refugees holding out by Lake Everstill have something gentle to wash down their rations.

item:charred-horn.text: Charred Horn. Charred Horns are the rugged, heat-baked horns harvested from youthful chimaeras dwelling in the crags of the Stonetalon Mountains. Tough enough to withstand harsh elemental forces, they serve as an essential tempering component in specialized armorsmithing. Harvested from fledgling and young chimaeras nesting across the craggy heights of the Stonetalon Mountains, Charred Horns are coveted for their unnatural resistance to flame and blunt force. The dwarven armorsmith Furen Longbeard, working from his forge in Stormwind, requires a collection of these horns to craft fire-hardened mail. Combined with venomous spider fangs from the Wetlands, phlogiston from Razorfen Kraul, and the galvanized horn of a chimaera matriarch, these calcified horns provide the core structural reinforcement necessary to produce an exceptionally resilient suit of protective armor.

item:chest-of-containment-coffers.text: Chest of Containment Coffers. The Chest of Containment Coffers contains enchanted receptacles used by mages to capture unstable magical phenomena. It serves as essential equipment for practitioners sent to investigate and safely trap unseen mana anomalies. Magical experimentation and sudden planar rifts frequently spawn volatile, invisible anomalies made entirely of arcane force. Standard physical cages cannot hold entities composed purely of magic. The Chest of Containment Coffers provides mages with specialized, enchanted coffers engineered to entrap and bind these subdued creatures alive. Kept near senior instructors such as Anastasia Hartwell in the Undercity and Jennea Cannon in Stormwind, the chest provides the necessary gear for initiates tasked with surveying anomalies before they can destabilize their surroundings.

item:claw-key.text: Claw Key. The Claw Key is one of three druidic keys hidden within the Talon Den atop Stonetalon Peak. Alongside the Barrow Key and Sleepers' Key, it is required to unlock the enchanted Talon Den Hoard. The night elf druids established the Talon Den high upon Stonetalon Peak as a sanctuary and repository for powerful relics. To ensure these treasures remained safe from trespassers, they hid them behind a layered security system. The hoard itself is sealed by three distinct enchanted locks: the Barrow Key, the Sleepers' Key, and the Claw Key. Each key is concealed inside a specialized druidic cache resembling a torch within the winding tunnels of the barrow den. The druids did not leave the keys unguarded or freely accessible. Opening the cache that holds the Claw Key requires first acquiring the Gatekeeper's Key, which is tucked away near the barrow entrance. Once retrieved, the Claw Key serves as a vital component in breaking the druids' seal and claiming the riches hidden deep within the mountain.

item:cloven-hoof.text: Cloven Hoof. The Cloven Hoof is a mysterious relic guarded deep within Thousand Needles by the Galak centaur tribe. Preserved inside an ancient sacred flame at Splithoof Hold, it emanates an uncharacteristic supernatural energy that tauren scholars are keen to understand. Held within an ancient brazier at the deepest recess of Splithoof Hold, the Cloven Hoof is one of the most treasured relics of the Galak centaur. The artifact is continually enveloped in a magical flame, requiring blessed water to briefly quench the blaze so it can be handled. Centaur society is notoriously brutal and splintered into violent clans, but their reverence for the brazier suggests ritual significance tied directly to their origins. Tauren observers like Rau Cliffrunner at Freewind Post believe the strange aura radiating from the hoof could reveal critical insight into the race that has plagued Kalimdor's plains for generations.

item:comar-s-heart.text: Comar's Heart. Comar's Heart is a macabre ritual component carved from Comar Villard, a faithful human wanderer searching the marshes of the Wetlands for his lost wife. Forsaken warlocks in the Undercity seek out this relic of pure devotion to feed the summoning rites of a succubus. To bind a creature as capricious and predatory as a succubus, warlocks must bait the demon with true purity and devotion. Carendin Halgar's disciples in the Undercity identify Comar Villard as one of the few men possessing such unblemished fidelity. While his wife was lost amidst the turmoil sweeping the Eastern Kingdoms, Comar stubbornly wanders the sodden roads of the Wetlands, refusing to abandon his search. It is precisely this unwavering love that marks him for slaughter, turning his still-beating heart into the ideal lure for a demonic servant.

item:corrupted-kor-gem.text: Corrupted Kor Gem. A Corrupted Kor Gem is a potent magical conduit warped by the dark rites of the naga residing around Blackfathom Deeps. Spellcasters covet such stones for their capacity to store sheer arcane force, though the gem's tainted state demands purification before it can serve righteous crafts. Kor gems naturally possess the rare ability to capture and contain substantial magical energies, making them invaluable focuses for sorcerers and enchanted smithing. Along the coastline near the ruins of Blackfathom Deeps, however, the resident naga oracles and tide priestesses claim these gems for their own shadowy rituals. Through foul enchantments, the serpent-kin warp the stone, suffusing it with malevolent, sea-borne corruption. While this infusion taints the gem's nature, the core latent power remains potent, drawing those in need of exceptional magical foci to harvest them from the naga.

item:courser-eye.text: Courser Eye. Courser Eyes are biological reagents harvested from the antlered coursers roaming the highlands of Stonetalon Mountains. Witch Doctor Jin'Zil in Malaka'jin seeks a large quantity of them to prepare a concoction he mockingly refers to as forest magic.

item:crate-with-holes.text: Crate With Holes. A portable transport container provided by the goblin entrepreneur Mebok Mizzyrix in Ratchet. Pierced with air vents, it safely houses a trained Snufflenose Gopher used to track down subterranean culinary delicacies within the quilboar stronghold of Razorfen Kraul. To acquire rare Blueleaf Tubers from the thorny depths of Razorfen Kraul, goblin merchant Mebok Mizzyrix relies on trained Snufflenose Gophers rather than blind digging. Because gophers cannot simply follow an adventurer across the dusty trails of the Barrens on foot, Mebok packs each critter into a well-ventilated wooden crate. Once brought into the humid, root-choked corridors of the quilboar lair, the crate is unlatched, allowing the beast within to follow its keen sense of smell toward buried tubers.

item:crocolisk-skin-classic.text: Crocolisk Skin (Classic). Crocolisk skins are harvested from the tough hides of the crocolisks inhabiting the islands and waters of the Loch in Loch Modan. Prized by merchants and leatherworkers for their durability, they fetch a respectable price despite the danger involved in securing them. The cold waters of the Loch teem with aggressive crocolisks that make their dens along the lake's islands and shores. Hunting them is no simple task, as these ferocious beasts possess razor-sharp teeth and thick, resilient scales capable of turning away careless blades. Despite the hazards, hunters operating out of Farstrider Lodge frequently harvest the creatures. Tailors, leatherworkers, and distant merchants continually seek out the skins to craft durable garments and protective armor, making a bundle of undamaged hides a valuable trade commodity in the region.

item:crocolisk-tear-classic.text: Crocolisk Tear (Classic). A Crocolisk Tear is a curious alchemical reagent gathered from the crocolisks inhabiting the waters of Loch Modan. It is sought by Chief Engineer Hinderweir to synthesize a neutralizing mixture capable of disarming Dark Iron explosives. Loch crocolisks are hardy reptiles native to the temperate waters of Loch Modan. While hunters often prize their skins and meat, Chief Engineer Hinderweir discovered an unexpected utility in their secretions. Combined with potent spider venom and resonant ogre minerals, the tear of a crocolisk provides the specific chemical properties needed to counteract volatile Dark Iron demolition charges threatening the Stonewrought Dam.

item:darnassus-marzipan.text: Darnassus Marzipan. Darnassus Marzipan is a festive confectionery crafted in the night elven capital for the autumn celebration of Hallow's End. Innkeepers in Darnassus hand it out to trick-or-treaters willing to dance for their sweet reward. During Hallow's End, the capital cities of the Alliance take part in lighthearted trick-or-treat traditions. While the dwarves offer sharp mints and Stormwind crafts chewy nougat, the innkeepers of Darnassus prepare delicate marzipan for visitors. Obtaining a piece requires visitors to showcase a bit of festive spirit—specifically, dancing on command for the innkeeper. The confection is one of four regional treats sought by young Jesper, a sick orphan in Stormwind's Cathedral Square who cannot go out to collect sweets himself.

item:divined-scroll.text: Divined Scroll. The Divined Scroll is an enchanted parchment used by the night elves of Silverwind Refuge to unmask the source of Ashenvale's disturbed waters. By channeling the residual magic within intact water elemental bracers, the scroll reveals the identity of the rogue spellcaster summoning them. The tainted waters of Mystral Lake have long troubled the Sentinels guarding Ashenvale. To pinpoint who is manipulating the water elementals infesting the lake, Sentinel Velene Starstrike provides travelers with an uncharged divining scroll. By gathering intact bracers directly from the slain elementals and using them as an arcane reagent, the latent bindings within the metal bleed into the parchment. The resulting Divined Scroll exposes the magical signature of the rogue wizard behind the infestation.

item:divining-scroll.text: Divining Scroll. The Divining Scroll is an enchanted parchment provided by Sentinel Velene Starstrike at Silverwind Refuge. Its magic allows investigators to trace the magical signature of the unnatural water elementals infesting Ashenvale back to their creator. When corrupt water elementals began rising from the pristine pools of Ashenvale, the Sentinels knew the disturbance was not a natural emergence. Sentinel Velene Starstrike acquired this divination scroll to identify the person responsible. By channeling the scroll's magic through intact elemental bracers as a focusing reagent, the user extracts the summoner's signature, transforming the blank parchment into a Divined Scroll that names the guilty party.

item:dusky-crab-cakes.text: Dusky Crab Cakes. Dusky Crab Cakes are a savory dish prepared by Chef Grual in Darkshire to satisfy the desperate hunger of Jitters. The local delicacy has a tangy flavor, and a famished Jitters considers it an exquisite meal.

item:elixir-of-pain.text: Elixir of Pain. The Elixir of Pain is an experimental alchemical concoction brewed by Forsaken apothecaries stationed in Tarren Mill. Distilled using blood harvested across the foothills, the mixture is designed to test biological agents intended to serve Lady Sylvanas's darker ambitions. The Royal Apothecary Society relentlessly pursues new formulas to bolster the Forsaken's position against their mortal neighbors and the Scourge. The Elixir of Pain represents one such trial, blended from freshly harvested ingredients collected around the Hillsbrad Foothills. Concocted with little regard for the living, the potion serves as a proof of concept for volatile substances intended to aid the Dark Lady.

item:elixir-of-suffering.text: Elixir of Suffering. The Elixir of Suffering is an alchemical concoction brewed by Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill. Developed under the orders of the Royal Apothecary Society, the draught is an experimental step toward a virulent plague intended to eradicate both living humans and the Scourge. Within the ruined hamlet of Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon tirelessly combines raw reagents gathered from the surrounding wilderness into toxic draughts. The Elixir of Suffering represents an early milestone in the Royal Apothecary Society's overarching mandate: formulating a new plague designed to exterminate the living and dead alike. Lydon tests the lethal brew on his unfortunate assistant, a frog named Umpi, to ensure its potency.

item:elune-s-tear.text: Elune's Tear. Elune's Tear is a rare, luminous mineral found on the central island of Iris Lake in Ashenvale. Revering it as a sacred blessing of the Moon Goddess, night elf herbalists and healers seek the stone for its potent ability to cleanse magical corruption and deadly sickness. Found secluded upon the small islet in Iris Lake east of Astranaar, Elune's Tear is a mystical stone believed to carry the purity of the Moon Goddess herself. The lake itself has not escaped the forest's corruption: its waters have turned a sickly green, and twisted bog beasts roam its shores. The stone is famous among local night elf herbalists and healers—such as Orendil Broadleaf—as an emergency remedy capable of washing away deep-seated corruption when ordinary woodland poultices fail.

item:emerald-dreamcatcher.text: Emerald Dreamcatcher. The Emerald Dreamcatcher is a sacred night elf amulet crafted to draw subtle vigor from the Emerald Dream. Bestowed upon Tallonkai Swiftroot by the druids of Ban'ethil Barrow Den, it was left behind in Starbreeze Village when the Gnarlpine furbolgs succumbed to corruption and overran the settlement. Crafted under the auspices of Gaerolas Talvethren, the druidic warden of the Ban'ethil Barrow Den, the Emerald Dreamcatcher is an enchanted relic given to only a chosen few. It is designed to siphon ambient energies directly from the Emerald Dream, blessing whoever carries it with fortune and protection. When Starbreeze Village fell to the maddened Gnarlpine furbolg, the amulet was left behind inside a dresser, stranded in the middle of hostile, corrupted territory.

item:empty-brown-waterskin.text: Empty Brown Waterskin. The Empty Brown Waterskin is an elemental vessel provided by Brine during a shaman's trials in the Barrens. Used to gather water from a nearby oasis, it serves as the first physical tool in learning the delicate, contested nature of water in an arid land. In the sun-baked plains of the Barrens, water is far more than a resource; it is life itself and a constant spark for war. The hermit Brine entrusts an initiate with this simple leather skin as the opening trial of the Call of Water. The task seems modest—carry the empty vessel down to the watering hole beneath her dwelling and bring it back full. Yet in drawing from that solitary pool, the bearer immediately confronts the harsh truth of the land: every drop of liquid is jealously guarded by local quilboar who view the oasis as an invaluable hoard, forcing the initiate to understand how water both sustains life and drives mortals to violence.

item:empty-red-waterskin.text: Empty Red Waterskin. The Empty Red Waterskin is a leather vessel entrusted to fledgling shaman during their elemental trials. It is used to collect fresh, untainted water from a surprising source in the plagued town of Tarren Mill. Given by the hermit Brine in the Barrens, this plain red skin serves a vital spiritual purpose in the Call of Water trials. Initiates are tasked with carrying it far across the sea to the Hillsbrad Foothills, seeking out the town of Tarren Mill. Though the town is occupied by the Forsaken and steeped in undeath, a lone well in its center continues to draw sweet, pristine spring water. Filling the red waterskin captures a vital sample of life persevering amidst blight, which Brine blends into a vial of purest water for the initiate's trial.

item:fel-moss.text: Fel Moss. Fel Moss is a tainted vegetative substance spreading through the forests of Teldrassil. Carrying demonic and corruptive energies, it is carried by hostile grell and grellkin and poses an insidious threat to the wildlife and native furbolg tribes of the World Tree. Teldrassil was planted to restore the night elves' immortality and heal the natural world, but corruption has already crept into its pristine boughs. Fel Moss is one of the most visible signs of this degradation. Found clinging to and carried by the impish grells and grellkin infesting Shadowglen, this malevolent growth radiates an unnatural, wicked magic. Forest protectors like the dryad Tarindrella have begun gathering samples to measure just how deeply this rot has infiltrated the sacred woodland canopy.

item:felix-s-chest.text: Felix's Chest. Felix's Chest is a container of personal belongings lost by the exiled gnome Felix Whindlebolt during the flight from Gnomeregan. Carried away by Frostmane trolls lurking near Coldridge Valley, it sits abandoned within one of their primitive mountain camps. When the subterranean techno-city of Gnomeregan fell to trogg incursions and toxic radioactive fallout, thousands of gnomes fled toward the snowy surface of Dun Morogh with whatever possessions they could carry. Felix Whindlebolt managed to escape the irradiated ruins, but amidst the panic of the evacuation, native Frostmane trolls scavenged the roads and overtook the scattered survivors. Felix lost his primary toolkits and belongings, with his sturdy chest hauled off to the crude camps the trolls maintain in the crags southwest of Anvilmar.

item:fey-dragon-scale.text: Fey Dragon Scale. A Fey Dragon Scale is a shimmering woodland relic harvested from the elusive faerie dragons living around Stonetalon Peak. It is sought after by the Darkspear witch doctor Jin'Zil, who uses it as an exotic reagent in an alchemical brew mocking night elven nature magic. Faerie dragons are mysterious, elusive creatures tied closely to the wild groves of Kalimdor, particularly the untouched forests around Stonetalon Peak. Their scales carry a natural magical luster reminiscent of the deep woods they guard. While revered by the night elves as harmless woodland spirits and allies, outsiders view them as an untamed source of rare magical ingredients.

item:filled-etched-phial.text: Filled Etched Phial. A Filled Etched Phial is an ornate dryad vessel laden with consecrated water drawn directly from a night elf moonwell in Ashenvale. Requested by the tauren of Thunder Bluff, this sanctified water possesses the rare spiritual potency required to quench the eternal flame shielding a sacred centaur relic. Obtaining this phial demands infiltrating night elf territory deep within Ashenvale. The empty vessel must first be claimed from the dryads around Raynewood Retreat, whose delicate containers are crafted to hold pure restorative draughts. Filled subsequently at a sacred moonwell near the western bank of the Falfarren River, the phial captures water brimming with celestial, nature-bound power. To the night elves, taking this water uninvited is an act of blatant desecration, but the tauren see it as a vital necessity for addressing a regional threat further south.

item:filled-vessel.text: Filled Vessel. The Filled Vessel contains purified waters drawn from the various sacred moonwells across Teldrassil. Entrusted to couriers by Corithras Moonrage in Dolanaar, it is delivered to Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm in Darnassus to aid his study of the World Tree's ailments. Teldrassil was planted without the blessings of the Great Aspects, Alexstrasza and Nozdormu, leaving its immense boughs vulnerable to unexpected corruption, strange beasts, and crazed furbolg tribes. In an attempt to monitor and cleanse the burgeoning boughs, night elf acolytes are dispatched to gather water samples from moonwells situated across the boughs. Corithras Moonrage consolidates these gathered phials into a single Filled Vessel, sending it onward to the capital. The mixture serves as a vital sample of Teldrassil's vitality for Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm, who works tirelessly in the Cenarion Enclave to uncover a remedy for the Great Tree's pervasive flaws.

item:flatland-cougar-femur.text: Flatland Cougar Femur. A Flatland Cougar Femur is a dense thigh bone taken from the predatory cougars that prowl the golden grasses of Mulgore. It serves as a vital component in a traditional tauren folk remedy used to counter lethal, venomous infections. The flatland cougar is one of Mulgore's most dangerous native stalkers, blending seamlessly with the dry brush until it springs upon unsuspecting prey. While hunters often harvest cougar pelts and claws for leatherworking and trophies, their heavy marrow-rich bones possess practical value in regional medicine. When Maur Raincaller, a tauren of Bloodhoof Village, suffered a venomous wound from the monstrous pink strider Mazzranache, he urgently requested a cougar femur alongside parts from other local beasts. The bone is crushed or boiled to extract its potent properties, forming an antitoxin poultice capable of drawing fever and necrotic venom out of a festering bite.

item:galvanized-horn.text: Galvanized Horn. A Galvanized Horn is a hardened biological growth harvested from the formidable chimaera matriarchs haunting the scorched crags of Kalimdor. Highly sought after by master armorers across both factions, this resilient specimen serves as a core material for specialized warrior armor. Chimaeras are savage, twin-headed beasts known for their ferocity, but the elder matriarchs that prowl the Charred Vale in the Stonetalon Mountains bear horns forged unusually hard by ash, flame, and survival. While standard fledglings yield brittle, blackened horns, the matriarch's horn possesses a naturally tempered strength akin to treated metal. Both the dwarven armorer Furen Longbeard in Stormwind and Orm Stonehoof in Thunder Bluff covet the horn, requiring it as a test of martial valor and as a critical ingredient in crafting exceptional mail armor.

item:gem-of-anacondra.text: Gem of Anacondra. The Gem of Anacondra is one of four dream gems held by the corrupted serpent leaders within the Wailing Caverns. Carried by Lady Anacondra, it serves as tangible proof of her defeat and the curbing of the Nightmare's spread over the Barrens. When Naralex entered his deep slumber to bring water and life back to the arid Barrens, the Emerald Nightmare invaded his thoughts and warped his closest disciples. Lady Anacondra and her fellow conspirators abandoned their traditional ways to become the Druids of the Fang, twisting their noble restorative purpose into a toxic delusion. The Gem of Anacondra is one of the four dream gems carried by these serpentine leaders, focusing their corrupted bond with the Emerald Dream and anchoring the nightmare within the cave system.

item:gem-of-cobrahn.text: Gem of Cobrahn. The Gem of Cobrahn is a dream gem carried by Lord Cobrahn, one of the corrupt leaders of the Druids of the Fang within the Wailing Caverns. It serves as both a focus of his corrupted reverie and physical proof needed by Nara Wildmane to confirm his defeat. When the night elf druid Naralex entered the Emerald Dream to restore the barren plains of Kalimdor, his nightmare twisted both the Wailing Caverns and his disciples. Among them was Cobrahn, who abandoned the peaceful ways of the Cenarion Circle to take the shape of the serpent. Lord Cobrahn carries one of the four dream gems that anchor the leaders' hold over the subterranean waterways, using it to channel the twisted dreams that threaten to transform the Barrens into a venomous marsh.

item:gem-of-pythas.text: Gem of Pythas. The Gem of Pythas is one of four corrupted dream gems carried by the leaders of the Druids of the Fang within the Wailing Caverns. Held by Lord Pythas, it fuels the nightmare twisting the subterranean oasis and threatening the Barrens. When Naralex entered the Emerald Dream to restore the arid Barrens, his noble vision was twisted into a living nightmare. His foremost followers fell with him, styling themselves the Druids of the Fang and seeking to remake the surface world into a venomous jungle. Lord Pythas carries this resonant stone, one of four dream gems anchoring the corruption within the caverns. The gem serves as a conduit of their dark design and proof to the druids of Thunder Bluff that Pythas's twisted trance has finally been broken.

item:gem-of-serpentis.text: Gem of Serpentis. The Gem of Serpentis is a dream gem carried by Lord Serpentis, one of the four leaders of the Druids of the Fang in the Wailing Caverns. It acts as a focal conduit for the twisted nightmare reshaping the cave network and threatening the Barrens. When Naralex's slumber inside the Wailing Caverns succumbed to the Emerald Nightmare, his most devoted followers were warped into the fanatical Druids of the Fang. Lord Serpentis is one of the cabal's four leaders. Like the other three, Serpentis carries an enchanted dream gem that anchors their collective will to the corrupted vision. Recovering this gem breaks Serpentis's hold over the cavern's ecosystem, striking directly at the leadership directing the corruption spreading across the Barrens.

item:ghost-hair-thread.text: Ghost Hair Thread. Ghost Hair Thread is a rare, supernatural material spun by Madame Eva in Darkshire. Infused with potent occult properties, it is said to bind spiritual energies and even sew life into inanimate things. The hermit Abercrombie requests it to ward his dilapidated shack against restless ghosts. Spun by the fortune teller Madame Eva in Darkshire, Ghost Hair Thread is far more than an ordinary tailoring supply. According to Eva, the spectral thread possesses versatile occult properties, ranging from binding malevolent spirits to stitching vitality into inanimate objects. Its ethereal nature makes it a valuable asset for rituals and wards in the cursed realm of Duskwood.

item:glowing-gem.text: Glowing Gem. The Glowing Gem is an enchanted stone recovered from the murloc camps along the waters of Ashenvale. Originally sought by the fallen scout Teronis, the stone is a vital component needed to reconstruct the magical rod crafted by Dartol. Discovered in the possession of the aggressive murlocs dwelling near Lake Falathim, the Glowing Gem is imbued with latent magical energy. The young night elf Teronis ventured out from Astranaar to track it down, aiming to piece together a tool capable of driving back the corruption seeping through Ashenvale's forests. Though Teronis met an untimely end at the lake, the stone itself survived intact among the shoreline scavengers.

item:gnoam-sprecklesprocket.text: Gnoam Sprecklesprocket. The Gnoam Sprecklesprocket is a sophisticated power supply salvaged from Sneed's shredder deep within the Deadmines. Gnomish engineers seek this component to supercharge specialized drilling machines in an ambitious bid to reclaim their fallen home of Gnomeregan. Found in a goblin shredder operated within the Defias stronghold, the Gnoam Sprecklesprocket represents an exceptional feat of compact mechanical energy. Operating deep in the lumbering machine piloted by the goblin taskmaster Sneed, this specialized core delivers enough sustained energy to drive heavy industrial logging and cutting blades. Its stability and potent output make it an invaluable piece of salvage amidst the subterranean tunnels of Westfall. In Stormwind City, the gnomish inventor Shoni the Shilent singled out the Deadmines shredder as the key to a larger offensive. Gnomish forces seek to reclaim Gnomeregan from the trogg hordes that overran it, but the sealed underground approaches present a formidable barrier. By harnessing the Sprecklesprocket, Shoni intends to power heavy gyrodrillmatic excavationators capable of boring directly through the solid bedrock surrounding the lost techno-city, establishing an unexpected underground assault route.

item:golm-fragment.text: Golm Fragment. The Golm Fragment is one of four missing pieces chipped from the Goaz Stone, an ancient relic uncovered at the Wetlands excavation site. Recovered by adventurers dodging ferocious raptors, it helps dwarven archaeologists piece together mysterious Titan inscriptions. Discovered at the excavation site in the southern Wetlands, the Golm Fragment is part of a monumental slab known as the Goaz Stone. Prospector Whelgar discovered the stone shortly before raptors drove the Explorers' League back, but found its inscription severed in four critical places. The Golm Fragment was abandoned amid the dirt and overturned crates when the dig was overrun, hidden away inside an ancient relic box until brave explorers could retrieve it.

item:heartswood.text: Heartswood. Heartswood is timber harvested from a sacred tree rooted within the Ruins of Ordil'Aran in northwestern Ashenvale. Born from the final resting place of two ancient lovers, its resonance with undying devotion makes it an essential lure for summoning a succubus. The Heartswood grows among the elven stones of the Ruins of Ordil'Aran in northwestern Ashenvale. According to legend, two lovers named Anathera and Latherion fell side by side during the catastrophic War of the Ancients thousands of years ago. On the very earth where they breathed their last, a peculiar tree took root, blossoming as an eternal testament to their devotion. Even millennia later, the wood cut from this tree hums with the memory of undying passion, making it an object of great curiosity for those who study emotional and spiritual bonds.

item:honorary-picks.text: Honorary Picks. The Honorary Picks are a bundle of ceremonial tools crafted in Ironforge for young dwarven mining apprentices. Entrusted to travelers by way of the gryphon network, they are delivered to Brock Stoneseeker in Thelsamar to mark his students' readiness to work the rich ore veins of Loch Modan. In dwarven society, mining is far more than a trade; it is a cultural cornerstone that keeps the great forges burning and the kingdom supplied with iron and stone. The Honorary Picks represent formal recognition for novice prospectors learning under Brock Stoneseeker in Thelsamar. Sourced directly from Ironforge, these picks are presented to students who have proven their dedication and are ready to tackle the open ore deposits across Loch Modan. Transporting the picks serves a secondary purpose for the mountaineers and merchants of the Alliance: introducing couriers to the kingdom's gryphon network. Ferried from Ironforge's Great Forge directly to Gryth Thurden and flown across the mountains to Thorgrum Borrelson in Thelsamar, the shipment illustrates how closely tied the capital remains to its outlying outposts through swift aerial passage.

item:incantations-from-the-nether.text: Incantations from the Nether. Incantations from the Nether is a grimoire of demonic magic held by the Searing Blade cultists lurking beneath Orgrimmar. Sylvanas Windrunner and her dreadlord lieutenant, Varimathras, seek to claim the tome to harness its fel knowledge for the Forsaken. Beneath the red stone streets of Orgrimmar, the Searing Blade—a subterranean sect tied to the Shadow Council—operates in the fiery tunnels of Ragefire Chasm. Among their darkest treasures is the Incantations from the Nether, a spellbook laden with demonic rites bestowed by agents of the Burning Legion. While the cultists use its vile secrets to plot treason within the Orcish capital, word of the text reached far across the sea to the royal quarters of Undercity.

item:invisibility-liquor.text: Invisibility Liquor. Invisibility Liquor is a potent, alchemically infused brew crafted using rare Crystal Kelp Fronds found in Elwynn Forest. Designed to render its drinker unseen for a brief window, it serves as the linchpin in a clandestine plot allowing two star-crossed young lovers to bypass their feuding families. The ongoing feud between the Stonefields and the Maclures makes peaceful contact between their households nearly impossible. When young Tommy Joe Stonefield seeks to meet with Maybell Maclure away from the watchful eyes of their kin, conventional secrecy falls short. Invisibility Liquor provides an uncanny solution: an alcoholic draught that bends sight around the imbiber, granting just enough stealth to slip across disputed farmland undetected.

item:jitters-completed-journal.text: Jitters' Completed Journal. Jitters' Completed Journal is a handwritten account detailing the grim tragedies of Duskwood, specifically the massacre at Sven Yorgen's farm. Fearing vengeance, the reclusive Jitters surrenders the finished text to clear his name and shed light on the sinister forces haunting the region.

item:jordan-s-smithing-hammer.text: Jordan's Smithing Hammer. Jordan's Smithing Hammer is a cherished family heirloom passed down to the human blacksmith Jordan Stilwell by his father. Its recovery from the haunted halls of Shadowfang Keep is essential for forging a holy weapon consecrated to the Light. To an ordinary observer, Jordan's Smithing Hammer might seem like mere smith's iron, but to Jordan Stilwell, it represents both heritage and destiny. Inherited from his father, this tool is central to Jordan's identity as a forge master outside Ironforge. Having somehow wound up within the forsaken stone walls of Shadowfang Keep in Silverpine Forest, it must be reclaimed before Jordan can attempt his masterwork—a sacred weapon fit for a holy champion.

item:logging-rope.text: Logging Rope. Logging Rope is heavy cordage vital to the Warsong clan's ongoing logging operations within Ashenvale. Shipments of this sturdy line were ambushed and stolen by local furbolg tribes who violently resist the Horde's expansion into the ancient forest. Maintaining the goblin-built machinery and lumber mills of the Warsong Lumber Camp requires massive quantities of durable logging line. Rather than reaching the loggers at their encampment, essential shipments were intercepted by the Foulweald and Thistlefur furbolg tribes. Driven mad by corruption and fiercely defensive of their ancestral woods, these furbolgs hoard the stolen ropes in their encampments across northern and central Ashenvale. Locke Okarr at Splintertree Post is tasked with recovering the misplaced logistical chain before the Warsong lumber camp grinds to a halt. Reclaiming the heavy rope directly from the furbolg den-mothers and warriors allows the Horde to secure fellable timber, bound logs, and rig saw machinery amidst constant guerrilla resistance from the native forest inhabitants.

item:lorgalis-manuscript.text: Lorgalis Manuscript. The Lorgalis Manuscript is an ancient text tied to the worship and lore of the Old Gods, preserved from the fallen night elven ruins beneath Ashenvale. Hidden within the sunken temple complex of Blackfathom Deeps, it holds secrets coveted by dark scholars seeking to awaken ancient, slumbering powers. The Lorgalis Manuscript rests at the bottom of Blackfathom Deeps, the sunken ruins where long-dead elves once dwelt before their city fell. Written by one Lorgalis, it speaks of the Old Gods who raged across Azeroth when the world was new and now lie chained and sleeping, and it praises Aku'mai, a servant of the Old Gods who dwells in the Deeps. Its lore is said to open mystical doorways and stir ancient entities that sleep deep beneath the world. Stored away in a pitted iron chest amidst the flooded corridors, it has drawn the attention of cultists and shadow scholars alike.

item:lurker-venom.text: Lurker Venom. Lurker Venom is a potent natural toxin harvested from the predatory spiders that prowl the rocky hills and woods of Loch Modan. Dwarven defenders require this caustic venom as a key ingredient to prepare an alchemical neutralizing compound against Dark Iron sabotage. The hills and crags surrounding Loch Modan crawl with predatory arachnids—ranging from common wood lurkers to the infamous matriarch Shanda the Spinner. While their bites pose a constant hazard to mountaineers and travelers, the explosives expert Ashlan Stonesmirk named their virulent poison as one ingredient of a disarming mixture, which Chief Engineer Hinderweir prepares. Combined with rare minerals and tears harvested from the loch's crocolisks, Lurker Venom forms a reactive solvent capable of disarming complex Dark Iron explosives.

item:menethil-statuette.text: Menethil Statuette. The Menethil Statuette is a rare silvery figurine portraying the late King Terenas Menethil II as a youthful paladin with an upraised warhammer. Lost in a shipwreck off the coast of the Wetlands, it is an exceptionally scarce memorial of Lordaeron's fallen sovereign. The statuette depicts King Terenas Menethil II in his early years, portrayed as a long-haired paladin lifting a hammer toward the heavens. Terenas was notoriously humble during his reign and disliked personal monuments, meaning few statues or likenesses were ever commissioned in his honor. Following the collapse of the Kingdom of Lordaeron to the Scourge, almost all such relics were obliterated, making this surviving effigy extraordinarily valuable to the Alliance. The statuette was cargo aboard the merchant vessel Blind Princess, bound for the Alliance harbor of Menethil. When the ship came under attack by aggressive Bluegill murlocs off the marshy coast, the cargo was scattered and the statuette ended up trapped in a half-buried barrel on the shore. With local threats like the Dragonmaw orcs hovering nearby, local defenders hurried to send the retrieved icon south to Stormwind City, where Highlord Bolvar Fordragon entrusted it to the Cathedral of Light.

item:mo-grosh-crystal.text: Mo'grosh Crystal. Mo'grosh Crystals are rare mineral formations mined and hoarded by the Mo'grosh ogres in northeastern Loch Modan. Prized for their unusual alchemical properties, they serve as a vital component in neutralizing Dark Iron demolition materials. Tucked away in the crags of northeastern Loch Modan, the Mo'grosh ogres excavate these distinctive crystals from their stronghold. Though the brute-strength ogres rarely specialize in delicate metallurgy, Mo'grosh Crystals are prized treasures among their clan, carried by common enforcers, mystic shamans, and their towering leaders alike. The crystals are relatively uncommon, making them a heavily guarded possession within the Mo'grosh Stronghold.

item:modr-fragment.text: Modr Fragment. The Modr Fragment is one of four missing pieces broken off from the ancient Goaz Stone, a relic unearthed in the Wetlands. Discovered amid relics and loose earth within the Whelgar Excavation Site, it bears ancient Titan script vital to assembling a forgotten prophecy. Before vicious raptors drove the Explorers' League from their dig in the Wetlands, Prospector Whelgar uncovered the Goaz Stone—a massive tablet inscribed with ancient Titan markings. Its translated text abruptly broke off across four distinct gaps, obscuring warnings of a divine plan and a doomed prophecy. The Modr Fragment is one of those four lost pieces, left behind among ancient relics and overturned soil when the diggers were forced to flee for their lives.

item:moldy-tome.text: Moldy Tome. The Moldy Tome is a water-damaged, salvaged remnant containing half of the original Tome of the Cabal. Lost in a shipwreck off the coast of Hillsbrad Foothills, it holds dark esoteric rituals coveted by warlocks seeking to master demonic summonings. The Tome of the Cabal was a singular, irreplaceable treatise on dark arts once held within the kingdom of Lordaeron. At some point in its murky history, the grimoire was ruthlessly vandalized and split in two. The portion now designated as the Moldy Tome was being transported south by ship toward Menethil Harbor and Ironforge. The vessel never reached its destination, succumbing to the treacherous waters west of Southshore. Swept ashore south of Azurelode Mine, the surviving half lay ruined by damp and surf amidst the scavenging murlocs that stalk the Hillsbrad coast.

item:mudsnout-mixture.text: Mudsnout Mixture. Mudsnout Mixture is a toxic alchemical base concocted by Master Apothecary Faranell in the Undercity. Created by blending a mudsnout composite with an alchemical colloid of decay, it serves as the foundation for the Royal Apothecary Society's deadly Elixir of Agony. When Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill seeks to craft a virulent new biological weapon, he sends a base composite of Mudsnout Blossoms, toxic mushrooms from the gnoll-held Nethander Stead, north to the Undercity. Impressed by the composite's potential, Master Apothecary Faranell introduces his own colloid of decay into the blend, producing the volatile Mudsnout Mixture. The solution stabilizes the mushroom compound while readying its virulent properties for further catalytic refinement back in the foothills.

item:musquash-root.text: Musquash Root. Musquash Root is a rare botanical specimen found only in the damp soil beneath the massive waterfalls of the Stonewrought Dam in the Wetlands. It serves as a vital component in a concoction brewed by cultists hidden beneath Stormwind. Musquash Root thrives in the perpetually mist-soaked ground where the cascade of the Stonewrought Dam crashes into the Wetlands. Its secluded and damp habitat makes it exceedingly difficult to harvest. While ordinary herbalists rarely seek it out, certain practitioners of the darker arts value the root for its potent chemical and alchemical properties.

item:neru-fragment.text: Neru Fragment. The Neru Fragment is one of four ancient carved stone pieces belonging to the Goaz Stone, a relic discovered in the Whelgar's Excavation site within the Wetlands. Unearthed from the disturbed earth, it holds a segment of ancient Titan script detailing the primeval history of Azeroth. Discovered by the dwarven archaeological expedition led by Prospector Whelgar, the Goaz Stone broke apart into four distinct remnants: the Ados, Modr, Golm, and Neru fragments. When raptors overrun the dig site, work ground to a halt, leaving the Neru Fragment buried beneath loose soil amid the aggressive beasts. Recovering this fragment is crucial for reassembling the tablet, allowing dwarven scholars to decipher a forgotten record whose surviving words mention a divine plan and a doomed prophecy.

item:ng-5.text: NG-5. NG-5 is the shorthand designation for Nitromirglyceronium, a notoriously volatile chemical compound. Procured for the gnome tinkerer Gaxim Rustfizzle in the Stonetalon Mountains, it serves as the essential catalyst for his explosive engineering schemes. Known formally as Nitromirglyceronium, NG-5 is an exceptionally hazardous chemical solution handled only with extreme caution—or reckless gnomish enthusiasm. Gaxim Rustfizzle, an operative stationed in the Stonetalon Mountains, requires the substance as a critical ignition compound. According to Gaxim, NG-5 provides the exact reaction necessary to detonate entire wagons loaded with dynamite, orchestrating a massive explosion meant to serve as a chaotic distraction against his adversaries in the region.

item:nightmare-shard.text: Nightmare Shard. The Nightmare Shard is a crystalline relic handed to couriers by Falla Sagewind after she examines a tainted glowing shard recovered from the Wailing Caverns. Containing the pure, disturbed essence of the Emerald Dream, it carries a troubling vision that prompts immediate warning and secrecy among senior druids in Darnassus and Thunder Bluff. When Falla Sagewind inspects the mysterious glowing shard unearthed deep within the Wailing Caverns, she realizes its energy is far darker than anticipated. Rather than mirroring the serene vitality of the Emerald Dream, the fragment reflects a twisting, unnatural affliction—a waking nightmare. Fearful of what its presence implies, she binds this tainted essence into the Nightmare Shard and commands that it be ferried straight to elder leaders of the Cenarion Circle without delay.

item:perenolde-tiara.text: Perenolde Tiara. The Perenolde Tiara is an emerald-studded heirloom of Alterac's fallen royal house, originally fashioned by dwarven craftsmen of Ironforge. Lost amidst the destruction of the kingdom, it eventually fell into the greedy hands of an ogre wandering the ruins before drawing the interest of collectors in Stormwind. Before the mountainous realm of Alterac collapsed in infamy and rubble during the Second War, its ruling house was the Perenolde family. Among their treasures was this delicate tiara, commissioned from master jewelers in Ironforge and set with brilliant emeralds. When Alterac fell to ruin following King Aiden Perenolde's treachery, the crown jewel vanished into the chaotic devastation of the high crags. Rather than being buried forever beneath the snow, the tiara was unearthed by Grel'borg the Miser, an ogre mage who rummages through the ruins of Alterac searching for abandoned wealth. News of the surviving relic reached Count Remington Ridgewell, a wealthy noble in Stormwind eager to acquire famous relics for his family museum, prompting a search to prise the tiara from the ogre's grasping hands.

item:plainstrider-scale.text: Plainstrider Scale. A tough scale harvested from the tallstriders roaming the sweeping plains of Mulgore. It serves as a vital component in a traditional remedy prepared by Maur Raincaller to counter a virulent infection. While plainstriders are best known for their soft feathers and lean meat, their powerful legs are covered in tough, protective scales. These scales are resilient against the harsh scrubland terrain and predator claws. Finding one intact and suitable for medicine requires patience, as only select plainstriders across Mulgore yield scales firm enough to be ground and prepared for folk remedies.

item:prairie-wolf-heart.text: Prairie Wolf Heart. A Prairie Wolf Heart is a vital organ harvested from the wolves roaming the grasslands of Mulgore. It serves as an essential ingredient in an urgent folk remedy prepared by Maur Raincaller in Bloodhoof Village to counteract venomous infection. The wolves of the plains are fierce predators, hardy and persistent across the sweeping grasses of Mulgore. Their hearts are sought out by Maur Raincaller, a tauren residing in Bloodhoof Village who fell victim to the legendary plainstrider known as Mazzranache. Struck by the creature's virulent, fever-inducing venom, Maur relies on traditional plains medicine to halt the spreading poison. Alongside other potent reagents like cougar bone and bird gizzard, the vital essence of a freshly slain prairie wolf provides the cleansing properties needed to concoct a cure before delirium proves fatal.

item:purified-kor-gem.text: Purified Kor Gem. A Purified Kor Gem is a rare, consecrated crystal required by the weaponsmith Jordan Stilwell outside Ironforge. Once tainted by dark energies, it must be reclaimed from the depths of Kalimdor and cleansed by elven magic before it can be forged into a holy arm of the Light. The stone begins its journey as a Corrupted Kor Gem in the possession of the vile naga lurking within Blackfathom Deeps, deep beneath the coast of Ashenvale. To cleanse the stone of its aquatic, shadowy taint, a paladin must seek out the night elf Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine. Drawing upon arcane and natural arts, Thundris purges the corruption from the stone, transforming it into the radiant Purified Kor Gem. Only in this pristine state is it fit to serve as a conduit for holy power. Outside Ironforge in the snowy crags of Dun Morogh, the human weaponsmith Jordan Stilwell requires the gem as a key component for forging a masterwork weapon. Having long possessed designs for an armament worthy of the Silver Hand, Stilwell lacked the exotic materials to realize his plans. The Purified Kor Gem, alongside Whitestone Oak Lumber and rare ore, provides the spiritual core necessary to channel the paladin's righteous wrath.

item:resonite-crystal.text: Resonite Crystal. Resonite Crystals are rare mineral samples mined by kobolds inside Boulderslide Cavern in the Stonetalon Mountains. Their frantic digging has drawn the concern of Mor'rogal at Sun Rock Retreat.

item:rough-quartz.text: Rough Quartz. Rough Quartz is a humble elemental stone gifted to novice shaman by a Minor Manifestation of Earth. Though small and unrefined, it serves as the vital spiritual core needed to craft a shaman's first Earth Totem. To the untrained eye, rough quartz appears to be nothing more than an ordinary desert pebble. Yet to a shaman communing with the spirits in Durotar or Mulgore, it is an elemental gift offered directly by a Minor Manifestation of Earth. The stone represents endurance, patience, and unwavering strength. When presented to an elder such as Canaga Earthcaller in the Valley of Trials, the quartz is bound into the carved wood of an Earth Totem, acting as the spiritual focus that links the fledgling shaman directly to the living soil of Azeroth.

item:rune-of-nesting.text: Rune of Nesting. The Rune of Nesting is one of the four sacred Relics of Wakening kept within the Ban'ethil Barrow Den on Teldrassil. It is an essential component in the delicate druidic ritual required to safely summon sleeping Druids of the Talon back from the Emerald Dream. Night elf druids undergo deep, cyclical hibernations within underground barrow dens to commune with nature through the Emerald Dream. Waking from this profound trance is not simply a matter of stirring; it requires a precise ritual guided by sacred instruments. The Rune of Nesting, kept safely within the Chest of Nesting deep in the winding chambers of the Ban'ethil Barrow Den, anchors this process. Alongside the Raven Claw Talisman, the Black Feather Quill, and the Sapphire of Sky, the rune serves as a conduit to call the Druids of the Talon back to the waking world. When corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs overran the Ban'ethil Barrow Den, the barrow's slumbering defenders were placed in immediate peril. Without access to their relics, the druids risked being trapped within the Emerald Dream indefinitely while invaders desecrated their sanctuary. Recovering the Rune of Nesting and its companion artifacts allows Athridas Bearmantle in Dolanaar to prepare the ritual necessary to safely awaken the endangered druids.

item:sapphire-of-sky.text: Sapphire of Sky. The Sapphire of Sky is one of four sacred Relics of Wakening kept by the night elves within Ban'ethil Barrow Den. It is an essential focus used to safely summon sleeping Druids of the Talon back from the Emerald Dream. Deep within the roots of Teldrassil, Druids of the Talon commune with the wilds while resting in hibernation within Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Awakening from such deep trance-states into the waking world is a fragile, perilous process. To safeguard the transition, the druids rely on four consecrated artifacts known as the Relics of Wakening: the Black Feather Quill, the Raven Claw Talisman, the Rune of Nesting, and the Sapphire of Sky. Without this resonant gem, the harmony required to call sleeping spirits back from the Emerald Dream remains incomplete, leaving them vulnerable to eternal entrapment. When corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs overran the barrow den, the sacred artifacts were left behind in their ornate repositories. The Sapphire of Sky resides secured inside the Chest of the Sky amidst the winding subterranean corridors. With the druids still slumbering as the furbolgs rampage around them, retrieving this jewel alongside its companion relics is an urgent matter for Athridas Bearmantle in Dolanaar before the sleepers are permanently lost.

item:shard-of-water.text: Shard of Water. The Shard of Water is an elemental remnant gathered during a shaman's communion with the spirits of water.
