Delivered to Islen Waterseer along the Barrens coast, it serves as tangible proof that an initiate has understood water's life-giving nature and conquered its corruption. For shamans seeking mastery over the elements, communing with water demands a deep understanding of balance, life, and preservation. In the trials of the Call of Water, shamans are directed to confront corruption seeped into natural springs—even journeying across the sea to blighted lands like Silverpine Forest. The Shard of Water is granted upon purifying these corrupted waters. Returning this crystal token to Islen Waterseer on the rocky shores of the Barrens proves the initiate's worth, providing the final key needed to forge their Water Totem.

item:shimmerweed.text: Shimmerweed. Shimmerweed is a distinct herb cultivated by the Frostmane trolls on Shimmer Ridge in the snowy heights of Dun Morogh. While the trolls harvest it for their own tribal rituals, local dwarven brewers covet its sharp, unique flavor for experimental ales. High above the lowlands of Dun Morogh, the Frostmane trolls tend patches of shimmerweed along the icy crags of Shimmer Ridge. The trolls harvest and store the plant in woven baskets scattered throughout their camps, relying on it to fuel their sacred and enigmatic rituals. Outside of troll society, few mountaineers pay the weed much mind, though its potent properties have drawn the gaze of inventive outsiders. In nearby Brewnall Village, brewmaster Rejold Barleybrew has taken a keen interest in the herb. Believing that brewing is in his blood, Rejold seeks to craft the ultimate dwarven stout and suspects that the pungent, unmistakable flavor of shimmerweed might be the missing piece. He frequently hires adventurous travelers to slip into the Frostmane encampments, dodge the hostile trolls, and haul back bushels to dump into his fermenting vats.

item:sleepers-key.text: Sleepers' Key. The Sleepers' Key is one of three enchanted keys crafted by night elf druids to seal their sacred vault within the Talon Den atop Stonetalon Peak. Kept safe inside a hidden cache opened with the Gatekeeper's Key, it is one of the three keys needed to open the druids' hoard. Carved into the heights of Stonetalon Peak, the Talon Den serves as a redoubt and sanctum for the druids of Kalimdor. Aware that their sacred relics and potent treasures might draw unwanted attention, the night elf keepers devised an intricate system of locks and hidden caches to protect their hoard. The Sleepers' Key is one third of that protective ward. Placed within a secluded cache in the den's depths, it can only be retrieved using the Gatekeeper's Key hidden near the threshold. Alongside the Claw Key and the Barrow Key, the Sleepers' Key must be set into the stone locks of the Talon Den Hoard to disperse the ward and reveal the ancient items held within.

item:snufflenose-command-stick.text: Snufflenose Command Stick. The Snufflenose Command Stick is a training rod provided by the goblin entrepreneur Mebok Mizzyrix in Ratchet. It is used to direct trained snufflenose gophers to locate and unearth valuable blueleaf tubers buried deep within Razorfen Kraul. Blueleaf tubers are coveted delicacies across Azeroth, but finding them is nearly impossible without specialized help. Buried in the thorny underground depths of Razorfen Kraul, the roots are entirely hidden from sight. To exploit this lucrative market without braving the quilboar dens himself, the Ratchet merchant Mebok Mizzyrix conditioned keen-scented snufflenose gophers to dig up the tubers. The Snufflenose Command Stick is the tool adventurers use to direct these trained critters, prodding them to sniff out and expose root nodes from up to fifty paces away.

item:snufflenose-owner-s-manual.text: Snufflenose Owner's Manual. The Snufflenose Owner's Manual is an instructional booklet from Marwig Rustbolt of Snuff Inc., kept beside the goblin entrepreneur Mebok Mizzyrix in Ratchet. It outlines how to deploy and direct a trained Snufflenose Gopher to locate rare Blueleaf Tubers buried in Razorfen Kraul. Written by Marwig Rustbolt, owner of Snuff Inc., this short guide details how to work with the company's trained snufflenose gophers. These beasts possess a keen sense of smell capable of detecting subterranean Blueleaf Tubers from fifty paces away. The manual instructs prospectors to release a gopher using a ventilated crate and guide its rooting instincts with a command stick, directing the creature through the hostile thorns and quilboar tunnels of Razorfen Kraul to secure the prized culinary delicacies.

item:spells-of-shadow.text: Spells of Shadow. Spells of Shadow is a dark grimoire carried by the Searing Blade cultists lurking beneath Orgrimmar in Ragefire Chasm. Filled with fel magic granted by the Burning Legion, it is targeted for recovery by the Forsaken leadership in the Undercity. Hidden deep in the molten caverns of Ragefire Chasm, members of the Searing Blade—a splinter cult tied to the Shadow Council—wield dark rites granted by demon masters of the Burning Legion. Among their most guarded treasures is the Spells of Shadow, a text containing insidious shadow and fel sorcery. Cultists and warlocks of the sect keep this book close at hand as they plot beneath the very feet of the Horde in Durotar. Word of the Searing Blade's demonic gifts reached the royal quarters of the Undercity. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and her dreadlord lieutenant, Varimathras, determined that such powerful relics were wasted on cultists with lesser vision. Varimathras tasks Horde adventurers with venturing into the chasm to seize the Spells of Shadow alongside its companion tome, Incantations from the Nether, directing their power toward the Forsaken cause against the Scourge and the Lich King.

item:stone-of-relu.text: Stone of Relu. The Stone of Relu is an ancient archaeological relic recovered from the Wetlands. Believed by Archaeologist Flagongut to be the key to unlocking latent powers within primordial fossils, it was briefly lost when local raptors ambushed the scholar on the road. Discovered during Explorers' League operations, the Stone of Relu is believed to hold the deciphering power needed to unlock prehistoric fossils gathered from Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. Archaeologist Flagongut identified the artifact as the catalyst required to unleash secrets within both his own Wetlands specimens and the fossil unearthed by Prospector Remtravel in Darkshore. While Flagongut was traveling along the Wetland roads to rendezvous with Prospector Whelgar, a pack of mottled raptors ambushed him. During the scramble, the relic was lost and swallowed by one of the ravenous beasts, forcing the League to enlist adventurers to hunt the marsh raptors and cut the ancient stone from their gullets.

item:stonetalon-sap.text: Stonetalon Sap. Stonetalon Sap is a sticky, potent substance harvested directly from the lumbering sap beasts that roam the craggy heights of the Stonetalon Mountains. It serves as a key reagent for the Darkspear witch doctor Jin'Zil, who uses its raw woodland properties to concoct a spiteful brew.

item:swoop-gizzard.text: Swoop Gizzard. A swoop gizzard is an organ harvested from the predatory birds soaring over Mulgore. Highly sought after for traditional folk remedies, it serves as a crucial ingredient for cleansing deadly toxins. Swoops are predatory avian hunters native to the plains and mesas of Mulgore, known for their keen eyesight and scavenging nature. While their feathers and meat serve everyday uses for the tauren, their internal organs—particularly the gizzard—are prized by herbalists and healers. When combined with other potent animal remnants like cougar bones and wolf hearts, the dense muscular organ aids in neutralizing venomous animal bites and halting festering systemic infections. In Bloodhoof Village, the medicine worker Maur Raincaller fell prey to the legendary plainstrider Mazzranache, suffering a vicious, venomous wound to his shoulder. Falling into delirium from the creeping poison, Maur relies on a swoop gizzard alongside a prairie wolf heart, a flatland cougar femur, and a plainstrider scale to concoct a curative poultice capable of expelling the beast's lethal venom.

item:tablet-of-verga.text: Tablet of Verga. The Tablet of Verga is an arcane stone inscribed with demonic runes essential for binding dark entities. Stolen by the sinister Burning Blade cult, it was taken deep into their lair within Skull Rock. Recovering the artifact allows dark practitioners in Orgrimmar to decipher the rituals needed to bind a voidwalker. The Tablet of Verga holds specific ritual runes required to summon and bend creatures of the Nether to a master's will. When the Burning Blade cult managed to steal the tablet, they concealed it within a hidden chest inside Skull Rock, just east of Orgrimmar. For the warlocks working discreetly in the shadows of the Cleft of Shadow, regaining the relic is crucial—not only to study its ancient markings for summoning a voidwalker, but also to deny the fanatical cultists their own dark advantage.

item:talisman-of-corruption.text: Talisman of Corruption. The Talisman of Corruption is a vile demonic trinket used by the satyr Xabraxxis to poison the minds of Darkshore's Blackwood furbolgs. Carried within the satyr's personal pouch, it serves as a magical conduit that binds the tribe to fel madness. The night elves of Auberdine have long struggled to understand why the Blackwood furbolgs turned so aggressively upon their former allies. Thundris Windweaver discovered that the tribe's downfall was not a natural descent, but deliberate sabotage orchestrated by the satyrs. Using talismans like this one, demonic agents project corrupting sorcery across the wilderness, tainting food supplies and twisting peaceful forest spirits into frenzied beasts. By channeling fell magics directly through these devices, the satyrs hold an unbroken grip over the minds and wills of the local tribes.

item:taming-rod.text: Taming Rod. A Taming Rod is an instructional tool entrusted to novice hunters by their trainers. Infused with simple binding magic, it allows a student to temporarily pacify and command local wildlife to master the fundamentals of beast handling. Novice hunters cannot immediately exert the mental force required to bind a wild creature to their will permanently. To bridge that gap, veteran trainers issue specialized Taming Rods. In places like Razor Hill, mentors such as Thotar give aspiring orc and troll hunters these enchanted implements to subdue regional predators—such as dire mottled boars and armored scorpids. The rod temporarily pacifies the beast, allowing the handler to practice issuing commands and fighting alongside an animal companion without the danger of an unbreakable primal bond forming prematurely. The control granted by a Taming Rod is fleeting, typically lasting only a short while before the magic fades. Each rod is attuned to specific types of wild beasts, serving as a stepping stone through successive trials. Once a novice has proved they can command various wild temperaments—from docile foragers to aggressive venomous hunters—the rod is returned to the trainer. Having demonstrated proper technique, the student is finally taught the innate art of taming, calling, and dismissing lifelong companions without needing an artifact.

item:tattered-manuscript.text: Tattered Manuscript. The Tattered Manuscript consists of loose, vandalized pages torn from the singular copy of the Tome of the Cabal. Hidden away in the dusty depths of southern Kalimdor, this battered portion of the text holds arcane secrets vital to warlocks seeking mastery over felhunters. The Tome of the Cabal was once an intact, unique volume safeguarded within the fallen kingdom of Lordaeron. At some point, an unknown defiler ripped almost half of the treatise directly from its binding. While the surviving spine and remainder of the book—now known as the Moldy Tome—were shipped south toward Khaz Modan and lost at sea, these torn parchment leaves drifted far across the Great Sea into Kalimdor, ultimately falling into the hands of the Galak centaur inside Splithoof Hold. Kept within a battered chest deep within the labyrinthine caverns of Splithoof Hold, the manuscript survived the harsh arid winds of Thousand Needles. Despite its fragile, tattered state, practitioners of the dark arts—both Alliance warlocks working with Krom Stoutarm in Ironforge and Horde practitioners aiding Jorah Annison in the Undercity—brave the aggressive centaur to reunite these lost leaves with the Moldy Tome. Once combined, the completed treatise contains the dark rituals necessary to summon and bind a demonic felhunter.

item:tear-of-the-moons.text: Tear of the Moons. The Tear of the Moons is a mysterious, radiant crystal unearthed by dwarven excavators at Bael Modan in the southern Barrens. Though prized by the dwarven expedition, it carries a volatile and corruptive power that led directly to obsession, exile, and bloodshed. Discovered during the initial excavations of Bael Modan, the crystal was celebrated as the dig site's first major triumph. Its strange radiance captivated the miners, but none more intensely than Feegly. Claiming the relic gifted him profound strength, Feegly fell under its sway. Fearing the artifact's dark influence—and alarmed by Feegly's increasingly unstable behavior toward his comrades—expedition commander General Twinbraid declared the stone cursed. Twinbraid confiscated the relic, sealed it securely inside his personal strongbox within Bael'dun Keep, and cast Feegly out into the Barrens wasteland.

item:tear-of-tilloa.text: Tear of Tilloa. The Tear of Tilloa is a delicate, pale blossom found in the shadows of Duskwood. Desired for its potent alchemical properties, it grows quietly in the overgrown grounds of the Mistmantle estate near Darkshire. Growing amidst the encroaching blighted woods outside Darkshire, the Tear of Tilloa takes root within the estate grounds of Stalvan Mistmantle. Though Duskwood's soil has turned hostile to wholesome vegetation, this small white flower persists among the shadowed plots. Its scarce growth and secluded location make it an object of interest for those seeking rare reagents not easily discovered in lawful markets.

item:tharnariun-s-hope.text: Tharnariun's Hope. Tharnariun's Hope is a specialized trap crafted by the night elf Tharnariun Treetender in Darkshore. Designed to pacify diseased wildlife rather than harm it, the device projects a calming light intended to tame rabid thistle bears so they can be examined for a cure. As a mysterious affliction spreads through Darkshore, the local thistle bears have grown increasingly frenzied and violent. Rather than sanctioning a cull of the afflicted wildlife, the druid Tharnariun Treetender crafted this unique trap in the hope of studying and curing the illness. When laid upon the ground, Tharnariun's Hope emits a soothing radiance. Any rabid thistle bear that steps across the trap's light has its frenzy temporarily broken, rendering the beast docile enough to follow an adventurer back to Tharnariun's camp for treatment.

item:the-book-of-ur.text: The Book of Ur. The Book of Ur is a scholarly magical treatise penned by the late Dalaran wizard Ur, detailing his research into strange extradimensional entities. Left behind in Shadowfang Keep, it fell into the hands of Archmage Arugal before drawing the keen interest of Forsaken researchers in the Undercity. Before Dalaran fell to the Scourge, Ur was renowned among the Kirin Tor for his esoteric investigations into other planes of existence and otherworldly creatures. Despite his fascination with extraplanar magic, Ur was guided by caution and ethical restraint, choosing to record his discoveries rather than recklessly breach the veil between worlds. Tragically, when the Scourge assaulted the violet city, his magical prowess and moral hesitations were not enough to save him.

item:thunderhorn-cleansing-totem.text: Thunderhorn Cleansing Totem. The Thunderhorn Cleansing Totem is a consecrated ritual implement crafted by Mull Thunderhorn in Bloodhoof Village. It is imbued with ancestral magic to purify the corrupted waters of the Thunderhorn Water Well. Across the rolling plains of Mulgore, the lifeblood of the earth is being fouled by unseen corruption. The ancestral wells dug by the tauren tribes provide vital nourishment to the herds and hunting grounds, but foul agents have tainted the water. Entrusted by the elder Mull Thunderhorn, adventurers carry this prepared totem north of Bloodhoof Village to drive out the pollution settling over the Thunderhorn clan's sacred spring. Through ritual invocation, the totem calms the disturbed spirits of the water and cleanses the ancestral site.

item:torch-of-the-dormant-flame.text: Torch of the Dormant Flame. The Torch of the Dormant Flame is a ritual implement carried by young Horde shaman during their communion with fire in Durotar. Awaiting the defeat of a flame manifestation atop the mountain, it serves as a vessel meant to capture primal elemental fire upon the Shrine of the Dormant Flame. A shaman seeking the favor of fire is entrusted with the unlit Torch of the Dormant Flame before ascending the peaks above Durotar. After drinking a spirit-revealing fire sapta, the shaman sees and challenges a Minor Manifestation of Fire upon the mountaintop. Slaying this elemental spirit yields a glowing ember, which is deposited into the weathered brazier of the Shrine of the Dormant Flame. Touching the head of the dormant torch to the resulting white-hot conflagration awakens the wood, transforming it into a burning emblem of elemental mastery.

item:toxic-fogger.text: Toxic Fogger. The Toxic Fogger is a specialized dispersal device filled with lethal poison, concocted by the Forsaken Royal Apothecary Society. It is designed to contaminate the Venture Company's air transit operations in the Stonetalon Mountains. Carrying a toxin brewed by Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill and dispatched by Apothecary Zamah in Thunder Bluff, the Toxic Fogger serves as biological sabotage aimed directly at the Venture Company's strip-mining efforts. Suspecting that the goblins rely on courier flying machines to shuttle messages and light cargo between Stonetalon and their headquarters, Zamah sends the fogger to release its poison right where machines land and refuel. Rather than engaging in prolonged skirmishes with endless mercenary crews, the Forsaken method strikes at the logistical spine of the operation, ensuring that the poison travels directly back to corporate leadership.

item:twilight-whisker.text: Twilight Whisker. Twilight Whiskers are harvested from twilight runners prowling the northern heights of the Stonetalon Mountains. In the settlement of Malaka'jin, Witch Doctor Jin'Zil covets them as an ingredient in a cruel, venomous concoction he mockingly names forest magic. The high crags near Stonetalon Peak are home to twilight runners, predatory felines attuned to the deep shadows of the ancient groves. While hunters prize their pelts, Witch Doctor Jin'Zil of Malaka'jin seeks their stiff whiskers for a far darker purpose. Seeking vengeance upon captured night elves who once defended these woodlands, Jin'Zil gathers components of the forest—resinous sap, countless eyes, fey dragon scales, and twilight whiskers—to brew a lethal draught intended to mock and poison his captives.

item:vial-of-phlogiston.text: Vial of Phlogiston. A Vial of Phlogiston is an alchemical substance used by master armorers to temper extraordinarily resilient mail. Guarded within the quilboar stronghold of Razorfen Kraul, it is coveted by both Alliance and Horde smiths forging specialized battle armor for promising warriors. Phlogiston is an intensely volatile, fire-bearing substance prized in esoteric metallurgy. Both the dwarven smith Furen Longbeard in Stormwind and the near-blind orc armorer Thun'grim Firegaze in the Barrens consider it an indispensable component for hardening warrior armor beyond ordinary physical limits. Without this alchemical agent, the specialized forging techniques required for Fire Hardened Mail or the Horde's Brutal Armor cannot be completed. Obtaining a Vial of Phlogiston requires venturing into the tangled thickets of Razorfen Kraul, located at the southern tip of the Barrens. The phlogiston is held deep within the bristling redoubt by the geomancer Roogug. Whether recovered for Furen in Stormwind or carried across the dust to Thun'grim's anvil, the substance demands a perilous descent into hostile quilboar territory.

item:vial-of-purest-water.text: Vial of Purest Water. The Vial of Purest Water is a sacred vessel blessed by the hermit Brine deep in the southern Barrens. Entrusted to an initiate shaman, its purified contents are essential for concocting the draught required to perceive elusive elemental spirits. Forged through trials of patience and cleansing under the guidance of Brine, the water sealed in this vial represents liquid in its uncorrupted elemental essence. Transported across the arid wastes of the Barrens back to the solitary shore where Islen Waterseer keeps watch, the vial serves as the vital component in brewing a water sapta. Without its pristine purity, a shaman cannot commune with the spiritual guardians that dwell in places far removed from the sunbaked flats.

item:warsong-axe-shipment.text: Warsong Axe Shipment. The Warsong Axe Shipment is a heavy crate of newly forged axes waiting on the docks of Booty Bay in Stranglethorn Vale. Ordered by the Warsong Outriders to sustain their harvesting operations in Ashenvale, it serves as a crucial link in the Horde's overseas supply chain. Maintaining the logging operations at the Warsong Lumber Camp requires a continuous flow of durable tools that cannot always be forged on the front lines. To keep woodcutters supplied, orders are sent across the Great Sea to the neutral goblin port of Booty Bay. Stored near Wharfmaster Lozgil, this crate contains sharpened axes intended for shipment back to Splintertree Post, highlighting the logistical hurdles the Horde faces in keeping its distant frontier camps armed and functional.

item:warsong-oil.text: Warsong Oil. Warsong Oil is a crucial industrial lubricant intended for the machinery at the Warsong Lumber Camp in Ashenvale. A vital supply shipment was intercepted en route by local satyrs, who took the oil to their corrupted woodland sanctuaries for foul rituals. The Warsong Clan's logging efforts in Ashenvale rely heavily on heavy machinery, goblin-engineered shredders, and massive sawmills. Keeping this industrial equipment running requires a steady supply of specialized oil. Without it, the clan's timber harvest risks grinding to an abrupt halt, stalling the flow of lumber desperately needed to build Orgrimmar and fortify Horde settlements across Durotar and the Barrens. Rather than reaching Splintertree Post and the logging camps, a recent shipment of Warsong Oil was ambushed by the satyrs infesting the forest. Instead of discarding the refined fluid, the demonic servants carried the containers into their corrupted enclaves—including Night Run, Satyrnaar, and Xavian—to use the flammable lubricant in their dark, detestable rituals.

item:water-of-the-seers.text: Water of the Seers. Water of the Seers is a sacred draught given to young tauren undertaking their tribal trials in Bloodhoof Village. Drinking the holy water near the tribal fire opens the mind to the spirit world, summoning an ethereal Plains Vision to guide the pilgrim on their spiritual journey. Prepared by tribal mystics, the Water of the Seers is an essential element of the ancient Rite of Vision. To pierce the veil between physical reality and ancestral guidance, the petitioner must drink the holy water before the central tribal fire in Bloodhoof Village. Once consumed, the potent draught grants spiritual sight, causing a ghostly guide known as the Plains Vision to materialize from the embers and lead the way toward Seer Wiserunner.

item:webwood-ichor.text: Webwood Ichor. Webwood Ichor is a fluid harvested from Webwood spiders prowling Teldrassil. Dirania Silvershine needs it, along with hyacinth mushrooms and moonpetal lilies, to brew an antidote for the poisoned Iverron. The Webwood spiders that haunt Shadowglen carry a venom dangerous enough to leave Iverron gravely ill. Dirania Silvershine asks for ichor from these spiders, along with hyacinth mushrooms and moonpetal lilies, to prepare an antidote.

item:whitestone-oak-lumber.text: Whitestone Oak Lumber. Whitestone Oak Lumber is a sturdy crafting timber sourced from the subterranean shipyards beneath Moonbrook. Prized for its strength, it serves as a critical shaft material for sacred armaments forged by Alliance master smiths. Found deep inside the labyrinthine Deadmines of Westfall, Whitestone Oak is shaped by Goblin Woodcarvers constructing the Defias Brotherhood's clandestine war fleet. Its dense, resilient grain makes it ideally suited to bear structural strain and high-impact wear, drawing the interest of seasoned armorers who require more than common ash or pine for ceremonial and martial craft.
